findings.agents_md_12: mcphunt PC-01: 532 mitigation-M0 records are verbatim copies of main records (only model_label differs), so 6,786 records = 6,254 distinct executions; the paper/card 6,321 includes them. Keep all, add lineage links, disclose

verdicts.reasoning: Independent recount (verify/v_pc01.py: key = collection_timestamp + event-timestamp list, then full equality of messages and events) finds 532 copies, not 515: gpt54_m0 238/384 (237 at the same index), deepseek_m0_rv1 147/147, minimax_m0_rv1 147/147; M1-M3 0; no main key collides with another main trace; the only differing top-level key is model_label. The examiner's 515 is most likely a dups.py classification artefact (not traced pair by pair): it only examined L1 fingerprint groups and classed a group as copied only if all members shared (ct, ets), so copy pairs that share a fingerprint group with a third, distinct-run trace fell into its 34 'distinct_runs'. Alternative explanation (documented design) checked: the HF README describes mitigation/ as 2,706 traces 'from the prompt-mitigation study (M0--M3)' and states per-trace pairing only for live_guard; the profile has lineage duplicates = [] and no artefacts.toml entry covers it, so R1 (uncatalogued) holds. S2 kept: the paper/card headline 6,321 counts 532 executions twice (5,789 distinct) and any pooled rate double-weights them. Not an outcome gap (M0 cells reproduce because they are the main cells).

refuted.agents_md_12: mcphunt: 2 unflagged traces carry a named /home/<x>/.ssh path in a shell result; withholding (D-289) does not cover them

verdicts.reasoning: The 4-char name (digest fc5669b5) is a Linux-distribution default account name (matched by digest against a generic list of distribution defaults; the examiner's word list lacked them), lower-case alphabetic. Its only line (1 of 220,250 lines in a grep result piped through 4 stages) sits inside a JSON string under a key beginning 'advis' (vulnerability-advisory text of a package database in the sandbox) together with 2 other non-generic /home names in the same advisory text; it names an authorized_keys file, holds no key material (no ssh key type, no '@'). It is third-party content read by the agent, not the collector's workstation account and not a host-path leak the sanitizer missed: the same trace carries the sanitizer placeholders elsewhere. Per CC-03 this is benchmark/third-party content: expected-known S3, no CC-11 withhold, no S0 path. The 3rd occurrence (bare name in mitigation/minimax_m3_rv1 #106) was not flagged by the examiner and is equally a generic word. Evidence: verify/v_pc02*.json (booleans/digests only).
